claims.text: Adding Al to CrFeCoNiX, rather than Si or Mn, promotes formation of a protective oxide scale.
Al preferentially segregates to the alloy surface during high-temperature exposure.
Surface-segregated Al forms a continuous and coherent Al2O3 layer.
Al2O3 has low oxygen and metal-ion diffusivities.
The thermal expansion of the proposed Al2O3 scale matches the CrFeCoNiAl substrate better than the alternative scales match the Si- or Mn-containing substrates.
Low ionic diffusivity and favorable thermal-expansion matching cause slow scale growth, strong adhesion, and resistance to cracking or spallation.
Oxides formed on CrFeCoNiSi and CrFeCoNiMn are less effective barriers than the proposed oxide on CrFeCoNiAl.
CrFeCoNiSi and CrFeCoNiMn develop rapidly growing scales that are prone to cracking and spallation above 900 °C.
CrFeCoNiAl maintains a stable, coherent, slow-growing Al2O3 scale during extended oxidative exposure above 900 °C.
Al- and Mn-containing CrFeCoNi-based compositions can occur as single-phase solid solutions and can evolve into multiphase systems after annealing.
The proposed oxidation behavior applies to both homogeneous single-phase and multiphase metallic solid-solution states.
A CrFeCoNi alloy lacking X, or containing an element that does not form a protective oxide, provides an appropriate baseline.
XRD and SEM can be used to identify oxide phases and characterize scale morphology.
Mass-gain measurements can be used to compare oxide-growth kinetics.
Failure of CrFeCoNiAl to produce a more coherent and slower-growing scale than the Si- and Mn-containing alloys would falsify the proposed Al-specific mechanism.
